title: SEBI Clears Automatic SWP, STP for Demat Mutual Funds
description: SEBI has now permitted automatic Systematic Withdrawal Plans (SWP) and Systematic Transfer Plans (STP) for mutual fund units held in demat accounts. Previousl.

faq.q: What is the difference between SOA and demat mutual fund holdings?
faq.a: SOA (Statement of Account) holdings are directly registered with the fund house or RTA, while demat holdings are electronic units held in a dematerialised account with a Depository Participant (broker), similar to shares.

faq.q: Will all brokers immediately offer this facility?
faq.a: While SEBI has cleared the mandate, the actual implementation will depend on the readiness of individual Depository Participants (brokers) and depositories (NSDL/CDSL). It's advisable to check with your specific broker regarding their timeline for offering this feature.

faq.q: Are there any charges for setting up automatic SWP/STP for demat units?
faq.a: Typically, setting up SWP or STP mandates does not involve direct charges from the fund house or depository. However, standard transaction charges (if any) or exit loads (if applicable) for redemptions might still apply as per the fund's offer document.

faq.q: How does SWP affect my tax liability?
faq.a: Each withdrawal through an SWP is treated as a redemption. The gains realised from these redemptions are subject to capital gains tax – either Short-Term Capital Gains (STCG) or Long-Term Capital Gains (LTCG), depending on the fund type and holding period.

faq.q: Can I set up an STP from an equity fund to a debt fund held in demat?
faq.a: Yes, once your broker implements the facility, you can set up an STP between any two eligible mutual fund schemes held in your demat account, provided they are from the same fund house.

faq.q: Is this change mandatory for all investors?
faq.a: No, this change provides an additional facility for investors. You can choose whether to set up automatic SWP/STP for your demat-held mutual funds or continue with manual transactions.
